headline: Telangana HC: Liberty to file belated GST appeal against Sec 74 order; no coercion for 3 weeks
reference: M/s Sri Laxmi Fertilisers & General Merchant v. Superintendent of Central Tax, Telangana High Court, W.P. No.39153 of 2026, order dated 20.11.2026
summary_points: Issue: Writ challenge to a Section 74 CGST/TGST order dated 19.12.2025, with the taxpayer claiming no show-cause notice was served, first learning of it via a DRC-13 notice.
Department opposed on huge delay, relying on the Supreme Court's decision in Glaxo Smith Kline Consumer Health Care (2020) 19 SCC 681.
Held: Court did not examine merits; petitioner may file an appeal with a delay condonation application and statutory pre-deposit within three weeks.
No coercive steps under the DRC-13 garnishee notice dated 06.11.2026 during the three weeks; the appellate authority to consider the delay and decide on merits if satisfied.
Practical impact: Writ relief for delayed challenges may be routed to the statutory appeal under Section 107(1) read with 107(4).
who_is_affected: Taxpayers facing Section 74 demand orders and recovery action who claim non-service of show-cause notices and who are beyond the appeal limitation period.
action_required: Where an order surfaces late, file the Section 107 appeal promptly with a delay condonation application, reasons and the statutory pre-deposit, and document the non-service.

social.linkedin:
Telangana High Court on a delayed challenge to a GST demand order.

The petitioner challenged a Section 74 CGST/TGST order dated 19.12.2025 for tax periods 2018-19 to 2022-23. It claimed it never received the show-cause notice and learnt of the order only when a DRC-13 garnishee notice was issued to its bank on 06.11.2026.

The department objected to the huge delay, relying on the Supreme Court's ruling in Glaxo Smith Kline Consumer Health Care.

The Court did not go into the merits. It allowed the petitioner to file an appeal within three weeks, with a delay condonation application and the statutory pre-deposit, under Section 107(1) read with Section 107(4). All grounds remain open in the appeal. The appellate authority is to consider the delay and, if satisfied, decide on merits. No coercive steps under the DRC-13 notice for those three weeks.

Takeaway: where service of notice is disputed and the limitation has lapsed, the statutory appeal with a well-documented delay explanation is the likely route.

Please verify with the official source before relying on this update.
